The fog had rolled in off the Blackwood Strait, thick and grey, swallowing the horizon until the lighthouse was the only thing in the world that existed. Elias Thorne, the keeper of the light, had spent forty years listening to the sea, but today, the sea was listening back.

It started as a low hum, barely audible beneath the crash of the waves. Elias, wiping salt from his spectacles, frowned. He adjusted the Fresnel lens, checking the rotation of the beam. The light swept across the water, illuminating nothing but churning foam.

Then, the hum changed. It became a rhythmic pulse. *Thump. Thump. Thump.*

Elias frowned, walking to the heavy oak door of the lantern room. He pressed his ear against the cold glass. The sound wasn’t coming from the water. It was coming from *inside* the lighthouse.

He spun around. The room was empty, save for the spinning glass and the brass instruments. But there, on the floor of the lantern room, was a faint, rhythmic vibration. The dust motes dancing in the beam of light were moving in unison, pulsing in time with the sound.

*Thump. Thump.
